title: The secret behind your cat’s kneading
topic: Why do cats knead with their paws?

lines: Ever wonder why your cat rhythmically pushes its paws into you?

beats.title: Kneading origins
lines: Kittens knead their mother’s belly to stimulate milk flow, and the motion stays with them into adulthood.
Adults use the same rhythm to stretch muscles and release feel‑good hormones, often before a nap.

beats.text: Paw pads hold scent glands, leaving a personal perfume on anything they press.
lines: The pads under a cat’s paws contain scent glands, so kneading also leaves a personal perfume on blankets or laps.
When your cat kneads, it’s showing trust, marking you as safe, and getting a cozy stretch.
Try gently massaging the spot they press – it can deepen the bond.

sources.claim: Kneading is an instinctive behavior derived from kitten nursing.
Kneading may also stimulate the cat and feel good, similar to a human stretching; it is often a precursor to sleeping.
Cats have scent glands on the underside of their paws, transferred when kneading.

youtube.title: Why cats knead – the hidden reasons 🐾
youtube.description: Discover the kitten‑origin, comfort stretch, and scent‑marking behind your cat’s kneading habit.
